units.name: Atlas AS7-D

tier.basis: The registry gives MechWarrior / BattleTech no tech tiers: its eras are periods of history, not gates a player unlocks.

cost_band.basis: The design has a C-bill price and a Battle Value on the BattleTechWiki, but the registry records no costs for this game, so it gets no band.

mobility.notes: Walks on two legs: the legs steer and the torso twists to aim. Pivot is the two-legs default and nothing in the sources gives a reason to change it; its heavy, ponderous feel goes here instead. The speed comes from the BattleTechWiki's tabletop figures for the AS7-D, as the registry asks: its top speed is a little over four-fifths of the Centurion reference's, and its cruising speed is lower still. The registry names no standard tank to compare it with; the sources say most other 'Mechs can outrun it. It mounts no jump jets. MechWarrior Online's stock AS7-D is a little slower again with its standard engine.

body.notes: A two-legged humanoid 'Mech with arms and working hands, topped by the skull-shaped 'Death's Head' cockpit that was designed to frighten. A hundred-ton design, the top of the assault class; the size examples put assault mechs in large.

armour.notes: Step 1 of the armour-class order decided: the registry's armour map makes assault 'Mechs heavy, and check A does not apply (body size large). Its armour weighs almost as much as a whole light 'Mech, making it one of the best-protected designs, and it is thickest on the chest front and the legs. Zonal is game-wide: armour is split by location, and wrecking a side torso also tears off the arm attached to it. Directional is coded because the BattleTechWiki describes the chest front as specially thick, so the back of the torso is the weaker side. The AS7-D has no ammunition protection (CASE); the later K model adds it to the side torsos.

sensors.notes: The registry says the BattleTechWiki gives no sight distances, so the band is the medium proposal. The stock AS7-D carries no ECM, probe or other electronics, and the standard sensors every 'Mech has give no trait. Its tabletop Improved Communications quirk lets it ignore the weakest level of enemy jamming, which only changes numbers. Its head can carry a small fold-away satellite dish for talking to orbit, which gives no sensor.

armament.name: Autocannon/20 (Defiance 'Mech Hunter)
armament.summary: The heaviest standard autocannon, in the right torso: one huge shell at a time with a pause between shots, enough to cripple a lighter 'Mech with a single hit, but only at close range. Fed from a ten-round magazine with no refill in the fight. The tabletop text says it lacks a cooling jacket and runs hot. Losing the right torso silences it.

armament.name: LRM 20 (FarFire Maxi-Rack)
armament.summary: A twenty-tube long-range missile rack in the left torso. In MechWarrior Online it locks onto a target and the missiles track it; ECM on the target spoils the lock unless a teammate holds a TAG designator on it. It can fire straight at a target in view or indirectly at one a teammate spots. Next to harmless inside its minimum range. On the tabletop the rack fires its missiles in four waves of five, and the bay holds twelve salvos; MechWarrior Online adds extra heat when too many such racks fire together.

armament.name: SRM 6 (TharHes Maxi)
armament.summary: A six-tube short-range missile launcher in the left torso, beside the LRM rack, firing a volley without any lock; hard-hitting up close. It carries fifteen reloads.

armament.name: Medium lasers (Defiance B3M) x4
armament.summary: Four medium lasers that back up the cannon and need no ammunition: each arm holds one and the centre torso holds the other pair. On the tabletop the centre pair faces backwards to discourage flankers; the MechWarrior Online page only places them in the centre torso. A laser's beam must stay on the target for a moment to do full damage.

crew.notes: One MechWarrior pilots it from the head cockpit, as in every MechWarrior title. The AS7-D is not an OmniMech, so battle armour can ride it only with magnetic clamps; riders cling to the outside and give it no seats (registry note). Tabletop dual-cockpit refits add a second crew member, but they are refits, not the stock design.

on_death.notes: Players drive it in MechWarrior Online and come back in another match or another 'Mech after it is destroyed. A tabletop pilot can eject by hand before the end, which does not count. With no ammunition protection, a hit to its ammunition can blow open the torso section holding it.

strengths.why: Its armour weighs nearly as much as a whole light 'Mech, so it soaks enormous amounts of fire and keeps shooting; one wiki likens it to a walking hill of plating.
The AC/20 can cripple a lighter 'Mech with one shot, giving it crushing close-range firepower.
The LRM rack adds reach: it can hit targets far away directly or bombard ones a teammate spots, so it is never without a long-range answer.
Four ammunition-free lasers back up the cannon; on the tabletop two face backwards to put off flankers, and in MechWarrior Online the centre-torso pair keeps firing after heavy damage.
Working hands and sheer mass make it a fearsome hand-to-hand brawler on the tabletop, with stories of it lifting and hurling medium 'Mechs.

weaknesses.why: Ponderously slow: most enemy 'Mechs can outrun it, so it can neither chase nor flee, and escaping it is the enemy's best hope.
Enemies aim for its right torso, because wrecking that section takes out the AC/20 and the arm attached to it.
Its cannon, lasers and short missiles are all close-range weapons; at a distance it has only its LRMs.
Its LRMs do next to nothing to targets inside their minimum range, so up close they are dead weight.
The cannon holds ten rounds and the LRM bay twelve salvos, with no refill in the fight; LRM ammunition often runs short.

countered_by.why: Fast 'Mechs pick their fights: they can outrun it to escape, or slip behind it, which is why it carries rear-facing lasers.
An ECM-carrying enemy spoils its LRM lock unless it closes to just outside minimum range or a teammate tags the target.

counters.why: Lighter 'Mechs struggle against it: its cannon can cripple one in a single shot, and in theory one Atlas can wipe out a whole battalion of light Stingers for little armour loss.
The BattleTechWiki's own example: one Atlas could in theory destroy a battalion of these light 'Mechs and lose only a little armour.

combos.why: A teammate holding a TAG designator on the target keeps its LRM lock, even through ECM, and lets it fire from out of sight.
A spotter that sees the enemy lets it give indirect LRM fire from a safe distance while it closes in.

units.memorable: The skull-faced hundred-ton assault 'Mech built so that fear would fight for it: a walking fortress whose autocannon can cripple a light 'Mech in one shot.
units.as_player: The slowest, toughest walker on the field. Turn on pivoting legs and twist the torso to bring the big cannon round on left mouse; the LRM rack on right mouse needs a held lock or a teammate's tag, while short missiles and lasers sit on other groups, two lasers covering your back. Watch the shared heat gauge and your ammo, keep allies on your flanks, and walk straight into the enemy line, because you cannot run from anything.

sources.title: Atlas, BattleTechWiki
sources.version: Tabletop AS7-D as retold from Technical Readout: 3025 Revised and 3039; page as edited 13 October 2026
sources.note: The Description and Weapons and Equipment sections retell the Technical Readouts in the wiki's words, so they are not official text. The page also lists the design quirks Battlefists, Command 'Mech, Distracting and Improved Communications, which the List of Design Quirks page shows only change numbers.

sources.title: Atlas AS7-D, MechWarrior Online Wiki
sources.version: MechWarrior Online; page last edited 1 November 2014
sources.note: The infobox places each stock weapon by location and gives each location's hardpoint types (ballistic in the right torso, missile in the left torso, energy in the arms and centre torso), which give each weapon's kind for step 4 of armament damage. It also gives the torso a limited twist and the arms a little more.

sources.title: Long Range Missile 20, MechWarrior Online Wiki
sources.version: MechWarrior Online; page last edited 19 June 2014
sources.note: Gives the LRM 20 the Missile Weapon type, a minimum range, indirect fire, a target lock that Artemis speeds up and ECM blocks, TAG spotting that restores the lock, heat scaling, and frequent ammunition shortages.

uncertain.note: Roles step 1 reads the Master Unit List role, but its site (masterunitlist.battletech.com) answered with a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403) and the old masterunitlist.info links return 404, so no official role line could be read and the role comes from step 5.

Anti-armour rests only on the LRM 20, whose cited pages name only enemy targets it locks onto (the 'Mechs of MechWarrior Online), so by the can_target rule it hits nothing but vehicles. No cited source calls any of its weapons anti-tank, gives one a bonus against armour, or carries official text on its targets.

Coded cannon by how it fires in the counted piloted game: the MechWarrior Online page says it cripples a lighter 'Mech in one shot, and that wiki's Weapons page (read, not cited for lack of room) says Inner Sphere autocannons fire a single shell. The BattleTechWiki's Autocannon/20 page (read, not cited) says the class fires its rounds singly or in bursts depending on the model.

Step 4 rests on the hardpoint type of the location each weapon sits in on the MechWarrior Online AS7-D page; that wiki's Weapons page (read, not cited) names autocannons Ballistic, lasers Energy and SRMs and LRMs Missile outright, and the BattleTechWiki's weapon pages give the same kinds.

Ranges rest on the tabletop long ranges in the BattleTechWiki's Autocannon/20, LRM 20, SRM 6 and Medium laser pages, read but not cited for lack of room: the AC/20, SRM 6 and medium laser reach about three-fifths of the reference AC/10's long range (short), the LRM 20 a little under one and a half times it (medium).
Banded medium from the uncited BattleTechWiki LRM 20 page's tabletop figure, just under the long edge, although every source calls it the Atlas's long-range weapon.
Banded short from the uncited BattleTechWiki SRM 6 page's tabletop figure.
Banded short from the uncited BattleTechWiki Medium laser page's tabletop figure.

The cited pages say only that it locks onto an enemy target ('Mechs in MechWarrior Online), so only ground vehicles are listed, plus naval by the naval rule; none says whether it locks onto vehicles, aircraft or buildings, or fires without a lock.

Coded rockets because no cited page says the SRM steers. The pages read disagree: the BattleTechWiki's Short-Range Missile page calls SRMs self-guided, its SRM 6 page says they lack sophisticated guidance, and the MechWarrior Online SRM 6 page calls them non-locking with only a minimal tracking system, while that wiki's Weapons page says only Streak SRMs track and need a lock.

The tabletop design faces the two centre-torso lasers backwards; the MechWarrior Online page places them in the centre torso without saying which way, and its strength text about returning fire with them suggests they face forward there.
Beam is the laser family default; the MechWarrior Online Weapons and Medium Laser pages (read, not cited) say a laser spreads its damage over a short burn that must be held on the target.
Directional rests on the BattleTechWiki's words that the chest front and legs are specially thick; no cited page gives the AS7-D's front and rear armour values location by location.
Naval is listed because the tabletop, a counted title, has naval vessels and submarines (BattleTechWiki support vehicle pages, not read in full); MechWarrior Online has none.
No cited page describes what happens when it dies; respawn follows the rule for a unit players drive in a game where they come back after dying.

The Atlas is a Star League design that the Clans also fielded as captured and retrofitted 'Atlas C' machines, so 'shared' could be argued; the given id uses inner-sphere, and the BattleTechWiki files the AS7-D under Inner Sphere houses.
MechWarrior 5: Clans, a counted title, was not checked for the Atlas, and the MechWarrior Online pages are from 2014 and were not checked against later patch notes.

fit_notes.note: The damage map turns every Ballistic weapon into kinetic, but the AC/20 fires heavy high-explosive armour-piercing shells (BattleTechWiki Autocannon/20 page) and the cannon family allows only armour-piercing or explosive.
The LRM locks on, but it also fires indirectly at targets only a teammate can see; the delivery order puts lock-on before lobbed, so the indirect fire lives only in the summary.

atypical.note: Step 4 of armament damage maps the AC/20's Ballistic kind to kinetic, which the cannon family's damage list leaves out; the family follows how the gun fires (one heavy shell at a time).
